data.cultural_impact: The name "Qiyam" holds cultural importance as it represents a person who is steadfast in their beliefs and principles. Historically, it is the name of the last Revelation in the Holy Quran that refers to the Day of Judgment, where every person shall stand before Allah to be accounted for their deeds. In the contemporary era, an individual with the name Qiyam might be perceived as strong-willed, determined and loyal, reflecting the positive connotations of the Arabic word, 'qaa'imah', which means "to stand".
data.spiritual_significance: On a spiritual level, the name Qiyam holds deep significance as it symbolizes being sincere and upright in one's interactions with the Divine, as well as with fellow human beings. It encourages one to be awake both physically and spiritually, and to strive for the betterment of oneself and the world around them. The Root of the Arabic word, 'qaa'ma', means 'rise' or 'stand up,' reflecting the idea of taking a stand for truth and justice, even in the face of adversity. Ultimately, the name serves as a reminder of the importance of fulfilling one's responsibilities in life and before Allah, in preparation for the Day of Reckoning.

islamic_reference.note: Traditional Islamic name with deep spiritual significance in Islamic culture

historical_references.reference: The Prophet Muhammad's (pbuh) prediction of the Last Hour and the Day of Judgement is known as the 'Qiyamah' or 'Qiyamah'. This is based on Hadiths (sayings and actions of the Prophet) where he spoke of the signs of the Last Hour and the events leading up to it. The belief in the Qiyamah is an essential aspect of Islamic eschatology and is a source of comfort and motivation for Muslims.

The concept of Qiyamah or the Last Judgement has undergone various interpretations throughout Islamic history. Some scholars and mystics have focused on the inner, spiritual dimensions of the concept, interpreting it as a process of self-judgement and transformation. Others have emphasized the external, physical aspects of the concept, focusing on the Day of Judgement and the events leading up to it. The belief in the Qiyamah has been a source of inspiration and guidance for Muslims throughout history, helping them to maintain their faith and hope in the face of adversity.

modern_usage.modern_context: Qiyam, an Islamic term for the night prayer, is experiencing a modern resurgence in various forms. The traditional practice of Tahajjud (voluntary night prayer) before sunrise is gaining popularity among Muslims worldwide. In addition to this, Majlis Qiyam (Qiyamul Layl, the night prayer of Laylatul Qadr) is being organized in mosques and community centers, bringing Muslims together for collective worship and spiritual growth. Social media platforms such as Facebook and WhatsApp are being used to coordinate and promote these Qiyam events, making them more accessible and inclusive for a wider audience.
